cleanIntro: Traditions asks for this before first use and after every shooting session. The NitroBolt shares the Firestick system with the NitroFire and nothing else about how it opens — it is a bolt action, the bolt comes out of the receiver, and the bolt itself strips into four pieces once it has been de-cocked.

steps.title: Treat it as loaded
steps.action: Point the rifle in a safe direction and handle it as a loaded gun. Wear eye protection before anything comes apart.
steps.quote: WARNING: WEAR SAFETY GLASSES WHILE CLEANING TO PROTECT EYES FROM FLYING PARTS OR SOLVENTS. NOTE: Reference to the exploded view diagram in the manual will help identify part names and numbers. RANGE/FIELD CLEANING AND ADVICE WHILE SHOOTING A systematic routine of cleaning while shooting is strongly advised to aid in avoiding problems while loading and to optimize accuracy. There are two ways Traditions® suggests effectively cleaning your NitroBolt® while shooting at the range. Method 1 Make sure the NitroBolt® is uncharged and unloaded. The safety should be in the second or middle position and the firearm should always be pointed in a safe direction. Take a Traditions® dry patch and saturate it in Firestick™ bore solvent (or you can use a pre-saturated cleaning patch.) Traditions® suggests using a Traditions® Range Rod but you can also use the ramrod that comes with the NitroBolt®. Place the patch over the end of your rod and insert it into the muzzle end of the NitroBolt®. Run the patch up and down to remove any fouling. You'll feel your ramrod stop at the shelf. Do not push past the shelf. Remove the saturated patch and discard. Place a dry patch over the end of the rod and run the dry patch from the muzzle to the shelf to remove any moisture. Do this until the patch is clean. Repeat this process as many times as necessary until your barrel is clean. Remove the bolt by rotating the bolt handle upward and pulling the bolt rearward while depressing the bolt stop until the bolt is completely removed.Using the NitroBolt® Chamber brush, insert the brush into the chamber and pull it back and forth. You may feel resistance. Repeat as necessary to remove fouling. You must be sure both sides of the shelf area are thoroughly cleaned so the Firestick™ is always fully seated. © 2025 Traditions® Performance Firearms. All Rights Reserved. 32 Method 2 Make sure the NitroBolt® is uncharged and unloaded. The safety should be in the second or middle position and the firearm should always be pointed in a safe direction. Using a Traditions® Range Rod (recommended) or the ramrod that came with the NitroBolt® with the jag removed, screw in a Bronze Bore Brush. Spray or saturate the bronze brush with bore solvent such as Traditions® Firestick™ Bore Solvent. Remove the bolt by pulling the bolt upward and rearward and depressing the bolt stop until the bolt is completely removed. Going from the chamber to the muzzle, run the bronze brush back and forth through the barrel. You will be able to go past the shelf with this process. The bronze brush will help break up fouling. Remove the bronze brush (and if using the ramrod that came with the NitroBolt® replace the jag so it is in the enlogated position) and place a dry patch over the end of the rod. Run the dry patch from the muzzle to the shelf to remove any moisture. Do this until the patch is clean. Repeat this process as many times as necessary until your barrel is clean. The same process should be repeated going from the breech. Do not push past the shelf. The chamber area may need additional cleaning. Using the NitroBolt® Chamber brush, insert the brush into the chamber and remove it. You may feel resistance. Repeat as necessary to remove fouling. You must be sure both sides of the shelf area are thoroughly cleaned so the Firestick™ is always fully seated. ADDITIONAL RANGE CLEANING ADVICE 1. Do not use shooting patches when cleaning your NitroBolt®. They are too small. You should use Traditions® cleaning patches. 2. If a patch gets stuck, remove the patch by removing the bolt and pushing it out with your ramrod from the chamber through the bore until it is out of the barrel. Never load with a lost patch in the barrel. 3. If unusual resistance is felt while loading your projectile, perform Method 1 or Method 2 to remove as much of the fouling build up as possible. NOTE: It should never be necessary to hammer or excessively force a projectile down the bore. Projectiles should load firmly with pressure from the ramrod down the barrel. If the projectile is the proper size, unusual resistance usually indicates a need to clean the bore. Use Method 1 or Method 2 to help remove fouling. If you are utilizing Method 1 with the saturated patch, it may be necessary to perform Method 2 with the bronze brush to remove excessive fouling. 4. When sighting in, it is important to develop a habit of consistently wiping the bore after each shot. This is beneficial when sighting in for hunting so that your accuracy will be based on a clean bore. Depending upon the specific load, temperature, and humidity, a short series of shots can be fired before it becomes necessary to clean the bore and breech area using Method 1 or Method 2. NOTE: A fouled barrel will directly affect your ability to group shots. However, in a hunting situation, only a few shots will likely be taken. If the barrel is prepped and lubed at the onset, it is not necessary to clean and lube the interior of the barrel between shots when hunting. © 2025 Traditions® Performance Firearms. All Rights Reserved. 33 18. DISASSEMBLY, DETAILED CLEANING & REASSEMBLY WARNING: WEAR SAFETY GLASSES WHILE CLEANING TO PROTECT EYES FROM FLYING PARTS OR SOLVENTS. WARNING: ALWAYS POINT THE NITROBOLT® IN A SAFE DIRECTION AND TREAT THE NITROBOLT® AS IF IT WAS LOADED AND CAN FIRE. WARNING: CONFIRM THE NITROBOLT® IS UNLOADED BEFORE COMPLETING ADDITIONAL STEPS THIS SECTION.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® NITROBOLT® — FIT-88 Rev 3 09-25 AKH — Section 18 Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning & Reassembly — p.34

steps.title: Move the safety to the middle position
steps.action: The rearmost safety position locks the bolt shut. Move it to the middle before you try to open the action.
steps.prose: This is a three-position safety, not the two-position button on the break-open Traditions rifles. The middle position is the one that lets the bolt move.
steps.quote: NOTE: When the safety of the NitroBolt® is in the third or last position furthest from the shooter, this is the ready to fire position. The action is locked in battery and the bolt cannot be opened. If your NitroBolt® is in the third or ready to fire position and you no longer want to fire, simply move the safety into the second or middle position. In this position you can now remove your Firestick™.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® NITROBOLT® — FIT-88 Rev 3 09-25 AKH — Section 15 If You No Longer Want To Fire The NitroBolt — p.30

steps.title: Eject the Firestick
steps.action: Rotate the bolt handle up and pull it back. The Firestick ejects as the bolt comes rearward.
steps.prose: The powder charge leaves the gun inside the Firestick. A bullet can still be seated ahead of the shelf after the Firestick is out.
steps.quote: 3. Rotate the bolt handle upwards and pull rearward. The Firestick™ will eject.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® NITROBOLT® — FIT-88 Rev 3 09-25 AKH — Section 16 Unloading the NitroBolt If You Don't Fire — p.30

steps.title: Remove the bolt from the receiver
steps.action: Open the bolt, confirm the chamber is empty, then hold the bolt release down and draw the bolt out.
steps.quote: 2. Open the bolt and inspect to make sure there is no Firestick™ in the chamber. Rotate the bolt hand up and pull rearward. Depress the bolt release and hold while pulling the bolt out of the receiver. Once you've determined the NitroBolt® is safe you can proceed with disassembly.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® NITROBOLT® — FIT-88 Rev 3 09-25 AKH — Section 18 Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning & Reassembly — p.34

steps.title: Remove the ramrod
steps.action: Pull the ramrod out of the thimbles and set it aside.
steps.quote: 3. Remove the ramrod from the NitroBolt®.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® NITROBOLT® — FIT-88 Rev 3 09-25 AKH — Section 18 Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning & Reassembly — p.34

steps.title: Wet the bore and let the solvent work
steps.action: Charge the bronze brush with solvent and let it sit in the barrel before scrubbing.
steps.quote: 3. Spray a bore solvent, such as Traditions® Firestick™ Bore solvent, on your bore brush. Note: Traditions® Foaming Bore Solvent can also be used instead of spraying the bore solvent on the bronze brush. Allow solvent to sit for 15 minutes inside the barrel. This will allow time for the solvent to engage and penetrate the fouling. Do not let it dry.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® NITROBOLT® — FIT-88 Rev 3 09-25 AKH — Detailed Barrel Cleaning — p.38

steps.title: Scrub past the shelf with the bronze brush
steps.action: Push the brush from the open bolt area out through the muzzle, then draw it back. The brush is what crosses the shelf.
steps.quote: 4. To clean your barrel, insert your bronze brush into the chamber area. Push the ramrod from the open bolt area to the muzzle until the brush exits the muzzle. Pull the ramrod back through the barrel towards the bolt area. The technique allows you to go past the shelf in the barrel and helps to break up fouling.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® NITROBOLT® — FIT-88 Rev 3 09-25 AKH — Detailed Barrel Cleaning — p.38

steps.title: Patch from the muzzle to the shelf
steps.action: Run dry patches in from the muzzle and stop at the shelf. Repeat until clean.
steps.quote: 6. Place a dry cotton patch over the jag and insert it into the muzzle. Run the ramrod with the patch from the muzzle to the shelf in the barrel to help remove fouling. Pull the ramrod back through to the muzzle. Repeat until patch comes out clean. WARNING: Do not push past the barrel shelf.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® NITROBOLT® — FIT-88 Rev 3 09-25 AKH — Detailed Barrel Cleaning — p.39
steps.warn: Do not push a patch past the barrel shelf.

steps.title: Clean the muzzle cap threads
steps.action: Take the muzzle cap off and clean its threads, its interior, and the muzzle threads underneath.
steps.quote: 7. Remove the muzzle cap (if attached) and clean the threads of the cap, the interior of the cap, and the threads of the muzzle. If you have a muzzle brake installed, be sure to follow all cleaning protocol for your muzzle brake.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® NITROBOLT® — FIT-88 Rev 3 09-25 AKH — Detailed Barrel Cleaning — p.39

steps.title: Clean the bolt area and chamber
steps.action: Work the chamber brush in to the back of the shelf and out, until the chamber and the shelf's back face are clean.
steps.quote: 8. To clean the bolt area, spray the NitroBolt® Chamber Brush with the bore solvent and insert it into the chamber up to the back of the shelf. Pull the brush back out of the chamber. You may feel some resistance. Repeat this process until the chamber area and back of the shelf is clean.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® NITROBOLT® — FIT-88 Rev 3 09-25 AKH — Detailed Barrel Cleaning — p.39

steps.title: Oil the barrel and extractor
steps.action: Light coat of gun oil over the barrel exterior and all metal, working oil in behind the extractor.
steps.quote: 12. Apply a light coating of gun oil to the outside of the barrel and all metal surfaces including the extractor. Tip: Push the extractor towards the muzzle. Apply oil into the space and release the extractor. This will allow oil to run down through the area.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® NITROBOLT® — FIT-88 Rev 3 09-25 AKH — Detailed Barrel Cleaning — p.39

deepSteps.title: De-cock the bolt before taking it apart
deepSteps.action: Insert the bolt backwards into the receiver, line the firing pin head up in the slotted groove, and press the handle down until it clicks.
deepSteps.prose: Taking the bolt cap off a cocked bolt releases the striker spring under full tension. De-cocking first is what makes the teardown safe.
deepSteps.quote: 6. You must decock the bolt before disassembly. Insert the bolt into the receiver backwards and align the firing pin head in the slotted groove of the receiver. WARNING: NEVER FORCE THE BOLT ASSEMBLY INTO THE BOLT CHANNEL. THIS CAN BREAK THE BOLT AND/OR DAMAGE THE FIREARM. 7. Holding the end of the bolt for support, use your other hand to put downwards pressure on the bolt handle so the bolt handle ends up in a downward position. You will feel a click or a stop. Your bolt is now decocked. You can also verify this by checking the cocking indicator is inside the bolt.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® NITROBOLT® — FIT-88 Rev 3 09-25 AKH — Bolt Disassembly & Cleaning — p.35
deepSteps.warn: Never force the bolt assembly into the bolt channel — the manual says this can break the bolt and damage the firearm.

deepSteps.title: Unscrew the bolt cap
deepSteps.action: With the spring tension released, take the bolt cap off with a 5mm wrench.
deepSteps.quote: 8. Now that the spring tension has been released from the bolt, you can disassemble the bolt. DECOCKED COCKED 9. With a 5mm wrench, unscrew the bolt cap.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® NITROBOLT® — FIT-88 Rev 3 09-25 AKH — Bolt Disassembly & Cleaning — p.35

deepSteps.title: Separate the bolt into its four pieces
deepSteps.action: Take out the firing pin assembly, bolt body and bolt handle assembly. Do not take the firing pin assembly apart.
deepSteps.quote: 10. Remove the firing pin assembly, bolt body, bolt handle assembly. Your bolt should have 4 pieces for cleaning. WARNING: DO NOT DISASSEMBLE THE FIRING PIN ASSEMBLY.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® NITROBOLT® — FIT-88 Rev 3 09-25 AKH — Bolt Disassembly & Cleaning — p.36
deepSteps.warn: Do not disassemble the firing pin assembly. That is where the manual stops.

deepSteps.title: Clean the bolt body and bolt face
deepSteps.action: Nylon-brush the inside of the bolt body and the bolt face with hot soapy water or solvent, keeping clear of the extractor.
deepSteps.caution: The extractor is a sprung claw on the bolt face. A brush dragged across it hard enough to bend it will cost you extraction.
deepSteps.quote: 11. Starting with your bolt body, use hot, soapy water or spray oilbased cleaner (we recommend the Firestick™ Cleaning Solvent) on a nylon brush or into the bolt body. Using the nylon brush, clean the inside of the bolt body and bolt face. WARNING: DO NOT DAMAGE THE EXTRACTOR.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® NITROBOLT® — FIT-88 Rev 3 09-25 AKH — Bolt Disassembly & Cleaning — p.36

deepSteps.title: Clear the firing pin hole
deepSteps.action: Run a fire channel brush or pipe cleaner through the firing pin hole in the bolt body.
deepSteps.quote: 12. Use a fire channel brush or a pipe cleaner to clean the firing pin hole on the bolt body.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® NITROBOLT® — FIT-88 Rev 3 09-25 AKH — Bolt Disassembly & Cleaning — p.36

deepSteps.title: Clean and grease the firing pin assembly
deepSteps.action: Brush the spring down its length while rotating the assembly, then grease its outside.
deepSteps.quote: 14. For the firing pin assembly, spray either a double ended cleaning brush or the firing pin assembly with the cleaning solvent. Using the brush, brush the spring back and forth in a downwards motion while rotating the firing pin assembly. Then brush straight down from top to bottom to help remove anything additional. 15. Grease the outside of the firing pin assembly. We recommend using a standard gun oil.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® NITROBOLT® — FIT-88 Rev 3 09-25 AKH — Bolt Disassembly & Cleaning — p.36

deepSteps.title: Clean and grease the bolt handle assembly
deepSteps.action: Nylon-brush the inside of the handle assembly and put a little grease in the notch the firing pin head sits in, and inside the bolt cap.
deepSteps.quote: 16. To clean the bolt handle assembly spray the nylon brush with cleaning solvent or spray cleaning solvent inside the bolt handle assembly. Use the nylon brush to clean insde the bolt handle assembly. Add a small amount of grease to the notched area where the firing pin head will sit for lubrication. 17. Add a small amount of grease inside the bolt cap.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® NITROBOLT® — FIT-88 Rev 3 09-25 AKH — Bolt Disassembly & Cleaning — p.36

deepSteps.title: Reassemble the bolt in order
deepSteps.action: Slide the handle assembly onto the body, drop the firing pin assembly in pin-down, and seat its lug in the lowest part of the groove.
deepSteps.prose: A bolt cap that will not start is telling you the firing pin lug is sitting in the wrong part of the groove — do not force it.
deepSteps.quote: 1. Slide the bolt handle assembly over the bolt body until it stops. Line the opening of the bolt handle assembly up with the opening of the bolt body. 2. Insert the firing pin assembly into the bolt body with the firing pin end down. The end with the cocking indicator should be facing outwards. 3. The lug on the firing pin assembly should go down into the slot of the bolt handle assembly into the lowest position of the groove. If it is not down into the lowest part of the groove, the bolt cap cannot be screwed on.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® NITROBOLT® — FIT-88 Rev 3 09-25 AKH — Bolt Reassembly — p.37

deepSteps.title: Tighten the bolt cap, then back it off one notch
deepSteps.action: Screw the cap down tight against the handle assembly, then loosen it by one click so the bolt can function.
deepSteps.quote: 4. Screw the bolt cap on until it is tight against the bolt handle assembly. You can use the 5mm wrench to help tighten the bolt cap. Once tightened all the way, loosen with one click or notch. This will allow the bolt to function properly.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® NITROBOLT® — FIT-88 Rev 3 09-25 AKH — Bolt Reassembly — p.37
deepSteps.warn: Fully tight is not the finished state. The manual calls for one click of backoff — leave it fully tight and the bolt binds.

cleaning.name: Barrel
tasks: Solvent-soak the bore for 15 minutes before scrubbing
Bronze-brush from the bolt opening out through the muzzle — the brush is the only tool that crosses the shelf
Dry-patch from the muzzle to the shelf, and stop there
Seasoning or lubed patch to the shelf from both directions
Clean the muzzle cap threads, its interior, and the muzzle threads
Light gun oil over the barrel and the extractor

cleaning.name: Chamber and shelf
tasks: Chamber brush in to the back of the shelf and out
Dry patch on the chamber brush, worked back and forth
Seasoning patch on the chamber brush, worked back and forth

cleaning.name: Bolt
tasks: De-cock the bolt before any teardown
Nylon-brush the bolt body interior and bolt face, clear of the extractor
Fire channel brush or pipe cleaner through the firing pin hole
Brush the firing pin assembly spring down its length, then grease its outside
Brush the bolt handle assembly and grease the firing pin head notch
A little grease inside the bolt cap

reassembly: Slide the bolt handle assembly over the bolt body, lining up the two openings.
Drop the firing pin assembly in pin-end down, cocking indicator facing out, with its lug seated in the lowest part of the handle assembly's groove.
Screw the bolt cap down tight against the handle assembly, then back it off one click so the bolt can function.
Cock the bolt: insert it backwards into the receiver, align the firing pin head in the slotted groove, and press the handle upward until it locks.
Withdraw the bolt and confirm the cocking indicator is showing red, then insert it normally so the firing pin head lines up with the receiver groove.
Reinstall the ramrod into the thimbles.
fncheck: With the bolt in, confirm it slides back and forth freely and the cocking indicator reads correctly. A bolt cap left fully tight will bind the bolt — the manual calls for one click of backoff. Do not fire with excess grease or oil in the bore.
